subject: chemistry
title: Graphene and fullerenes
key_idea: Graphene is a single layer of graphite. Fullerenes are hollow molecules of carbon atoms, including buckminsterfullerene (C60) and carbon nanotubes. Their bonding is based on hexagonal rings of carbon atoms, and their properties make them useful in electronics and materials.

blocks.text: Graphene is a form of carbon that is just one atom thick.

items.meaning: A single layer of graphite, one atom thick.
An electron that is not held in a bond and is free to move through the structure.

items: Each carbon atom forms **three covalent bonds** with three other carbon atoms.
The atoms form hexagonal rings in a single layer.
One electron from each carbon atom is delocalised.
The delocalised electrons can move through the structure and carry charge, so graphene conducts electricity.
The covalent bonds are strong, so graphene is very strong.
Graphene is a single layer of graphite with hexagonal rings.
It conducts electricity because of delocalised electrons, and is strong because of its covalent bonds.

blocks.text: Fullerenes are molecules of carbon atoms with hollow shapes.

items: Their structure is based on hexagonal rings of carbon atoms.
They may also contain rings with five or seven carbon atoms.
The first fullerene discovered was **buckminsterfullerene (C60)**. It has a spherical shape.
**Carbon nanotubes** are cylindrical fullerenes. They have a very high length to diameter ratio.
A carbon nanotube has bonding like graphene, so it also has delocalised electrons and conducts electricity.

parts.name: Graphene
parts.detail: A single layer of graphite. Each carbon atom forms three bonds. Delocalised electrons make it a good conductor. Useful in electronics and composites.

parts.name: Buckminsterfullerene
parts.detail: C60. A hollow sphere of carbon atoms based on hexagonal rings, with some rings of five carbon atoms. It was the first fullerene discovered.

parts.name: Carbon nanotube
parts.detail: A cylindrical fullerene with a very high length to diameter ratio. It has delocalised electrons, so it conducts electricity. Useful in nanotechnology, electronics and materials.

parts.name: Fullerene
parts.detail: A molecule of carbon atoms with a hollow shape. Uses include drug delivery, catalysts, lubricants and strengthening materials.

items: Fullerenes are hollow molecules of carbon atoms based on hexagonal rings.
C60 is spherical. Nanotubes are cylindrical with a very high length to diameter ratio.

blocks.text: Each use follows from a property that comes from the structure.

rows: Conduct electricity, very high length to diameter ratio
Drug delivery, catalysts, lubricants, hydrogen storage

items: Graphene and nanotubes are used in electronics because they conduct electricity.
Hollow fullerene shapes are used in drug delivery.

exam_phrases: each carbon atom forms three covalent bonds
one electron from each carbon atom is delocalised
delocalised electrons carry (electrical) charge through the structure

mistakes.wrong: Carbon nanotubes conduct electricity because they carry electricity or current through the nanotube.
mistakes.right: Current and electricity are ignored. Say delocalised electrons carry (electrical) charge through the structure.

mistakes.wrong: Carbon nanotubes conduct because they contain ions.
mistakes.right: Nanotubes contain delocalised electrons, one from each carbon atom. They have no ions.

worked_example.question:
Carbon nanotubes are cylindrical fullerenes.

Explain why carbon nanotubes can conduct electricity.

Refer to bonding between carbon atoms in your answer.
answer_points: Each carbon atom forms three covalent bonds.
So one electron from each carbon atom is delocalised.
So these delocalised electrons carry electrical charge through the structure (nanotube).
worked_example.tip: One mark each. Start from the bonding, because the question asks about it.

exam_phrases: each carbon atom joined to three others
one electron free to move / delocalised
reject reference to movement of ions

mistakes.wrong: Graphene conducts because its ions can move.
mistakes.right: Reference to the movement of ions is rejected. Say one electron from each carbon atom is free to move (delocalised).

mistakes.wrong: Graphene and a fullerene both have giant covalent structures.
mistakes.right: Graphene has a giant covalent structure. A fullerene has a molecular structure, with weak forces between its molecules.

worked_example.question: Explain why graphene will be a good conductor of an electric current.
answer_points: Carbon has four outer shell electrons.
Three electrons are used in bonds with other carbon atoms (each carbon atom forms three bonds).
One electron is free to move (it is delocalised).
worked_example.tip: Each carbon atom having one electron not involved in bonding also scores. Do not refer to ions moving.

exam_phrases: conducts electricity because touchscreens need to be able to conduct electricity
high strength so screen does not break
transparent so can see light through the display

mistakes.wrong: Graphene is suitable for touchscreens because it is cheap.
mistakes.right: Use the table. Graphene has a high cost, so choose the useful properties: it conducts electricity, is strong and is transparent.

mistakes.wrong: Graphene is the same as graphite because both are carbon.
mistakes.right: Graphene is a single layer of graphite, one atom thick. It is a different allotrope of carbon.

worked_example.question:
Graphene is a single layer of graphite. It is just one atom thick. Graphene can be used to make touchscreens for electronic devices.

The table shows some properties of graphite and graphene.

Graphite: cost low, electrical conductivity high, density low, strength low, colour black.
Graphene: cost high, electrical conductivity high, density low, strength high, colour transparent.

Explain why graphene is suitable for making touchscreens.

Use the information from the table.
answer_points: It conducts electricity, because touchscreens need to conduct electricity.
It has high strength, so the screen does not break easily or wear off.
It is transparent, so you can see light through the display.
worked_example.tip: Link each property to what a touchscreen needs.
